newsitem.title: GERMANY: German meat consumption down 8 percent since 1990.
newsitem.headline: German meat consumption down 8 percent since 1990.

text.p: German meat consumption dropped to 61 kg per person in 1996, a fall of eight percent since 1990, with beef hit most after last year's "mad cow disease" scare, according to a survey released on Wednesday.
Beef consumption fell by 4.3 kg per person to 10.5 kg over the last six years. Germans apparently replaced it with poultry, with annual per capita consumption of poultry up 1.5 kg at 8.5.
Pork consumption was fairly stable, the survey by the Central Marketing Society of German Agriculture survey found.

In March last year the British government sparked a slump in European beef consumption by admitting a likely link between the "mad cow" disease BSE and its deadly brain-wasting equivalent in humans, Creutzfeld-Jakob Disease (CJD).
German beef consumption slumped by up to 40 percent in the wake of the announcement and then recovered somewhat.
The survey said since the March announcement 98 percent of Germans said they preferred home-produced beef, compared with 82 percent in October 1994.
